guideTitle: 5 Best Floor Lamps With USB Ports (2026)
metaTitle: Best Floor Lamps With USB Ports (2026)
metaDescription: Five floor lamps with built-in USB and Type-C charging compared on port count, outlets, shelves and table space for a chair or sofa side.
mainKeyword: best floor lamps with usb ports
introParagraphs: A floor lamp with charging ports puts light and power in the same spot, which is handy beside a recliner, a sofa end or a bed where outlets are never close enough. The five lamps here all pair a shaded LED bulb with built-in USB charging, and most add shelves or a tabletop. The runjuly offers the biggest port count with two USB ports, one Type-C port and two AC outlets, while the SUNMORY has two USB ports and two outlets and the Coucrek keeps it simple with one USB and one Type-C port.

The spread in layout is wide. The runjuly and ONEWISH are lamp-and-table combos, the ONEWISH with a round tabletop that saves floor space compared with a rectangular table, the SUNMORY and FOLKSMATE are shelf lamps with a drawer or three tiers, and the Coucrek is a multi-tier shelf lamp with a bulb that switches among three color temperatures. Bulbs range from a 9W 800 lumen LED in the SUNMORY to an 11W bulb in the Coucrek.

We evaluated each lamp on how many devices it can charge at once, how stable and reachable its shelves or table are, how adjustable the light is, and how easy assembly looks, based on product specs and buyer feedback. For active adults we favored clear, labeled ports at a reachable height over decorative extras.

products.name: runjuly Floor Lamp with Table and Charging Station
products.description:
The runjuly is a true lamp-and-table combo, which means it replaces an end table instead of sitting next to one. The integrated power hub provides two USB ports, one Type-C port and two AC outlets, so five devices can be powered at once. A roomy desktop holds a phone and daily essentials, and a wood drawer adds hidden storage.

The 180 degree rotatable linen shade lets you aim soft, glare-free light where you need it. The tradeoff is size and cost, because a narrow side table with a drawer takes more room than a slim pole and sits in the highest cost tier here. It also brings a heavier assembly job than a simple pole lamp, so expect to set aside some time.

Once built, it is the most convenient setup for a sofa arm or bedside, because your phone, tablet and a small appliance can all charge within reach. Compared with the Coucrek's one USB and one Type-C port, the runjuly has far more connection options. We rank it first because the combination of ports, outlets, surface and drawer solves the most real problems at once.

products.name: SUNMORY Floor Lamp with Shelves and Drawer
products.description:
The SUNMORY combines open shelves and a drawer with a lamp, and it charges four devices at once through two USB ports and two power outlets. A 9W, 800 lumen LED bulb is included, with three color temperatures and a listed life of 30,000 hours. The shelves are made of solid wood, and the wood grain is visible, which gives it a furniture look.

The tradeoff is that shelves are for light display and storage, not for heavy loads, so keep books and larger items on lower tiers. The bulb is moderate in brightness, so it works better as ambient light than as a bright task lamp. The cost sits in a middle tier, making it cheaper than the runjuly but a step above the simplest lamps.

Because the ports are on the lamp, the cables run along the shelves, so plan cable routing so cords do not hang into a walkway. Compared with the Coucrek, it offers more outlets and a drawer, while the Coucrek offers fewer ports at a lower tier. It is a good choice for a corner chair or a living room wall.
products.bestFor: A reading corner that needs shelves and four charge points
pros: Two USB ports plus two outlets
Solid wood shelves with a drawer
Bulb included with three color temperatures
cons: Shelves are not for heavy loads
Cables need routing along the shelves

products.name: ONEWISH Floor Lamp with Round Table and Charging Station
products.description:
The ONEWISH uses a small round table beneath its lamp, and the listing says it saves 15 to 20 percent more floor space than rectangular tables of similar seating capacity. The round shape has no sharp corners, which makes walking past it smoother. It offers a 5V/2A USB port, a Type-C port and an AC socket.

Its LED bulb offers 3000K, 4500K and 6500K color temperatures and is listed for more than 10,000 hours of life. The linen shade softens the light. The tradeoff is fewer connection points than the runjuly or SUNMORY, so a household with several devices to charge may run out of ports.

The round table keeps essentials like a phone, glasses and a drink within reach without taking much room, which suits small living rooms. It sits at an upper mid-range cost tier. Compared with the runjuly, it trades connection count for a more compact shape, and we would choose it for narrow spaces beside a recliner.
products.bestFor: Small rooms where a round table is easier to navigate
pros: Round table with no sharp corners
cons: Fewer ports than the runjuly or SUNMORY
Small tabletop holds only a few items

products.name: FOLKSMATE Floor Lamp with Shelves and Touch Control

specList.label: Ports
specList.value: 2 USB 5V/2A, Type-C and a power outlet

products.description:
The FOLKSMATE is a three-tier shelf lamp with a sturdy wooden frame and a fabric shade. Its touch control gives three-way dimming in soft, natural and high settings, and the charging side offers two fast-charging 5V/2A USB ports, a Type-C port and a power outlet. That is a flexible set of connections in a slim corner design.

The tradeoff is touch control, which some users find less reliable than a physical switch, especially with dry skin. The shelves suit small display items and accessories rather than heavy loads. It sits at a lower mid-range cost tier, so it is a good value for what it offers.

Assembly is straightforward for a shelf lamp, with a square footprint that tucks into a corner. Compared with the SUNMORY, it offers touch dimming instead of a drawer. We would choose it for a corner where you want a simple, dimmable light and a few charge points.
products.bestFor: A tidy corner with simple touch dimming
pros: Two fast USB ports plus Type-C
cons: Touch control suits some users less

products.name: Coucrek Shelf Floor Lamp with Charging Station
products.description:
The Coucrek is the simplest and lowest-cost lamp in this comparison. It has open multi-tier shelves, one USB port and one Type-C port, and an 11W bulb that switches among 3000K warm white, 4000K natural white and a cooler setting. The 11W bulb is the highest wattage among the shelf lamps here.

The limited ports are the tradeoff. With only two charge points and no AC outlet, it handles a phone and a tablet but not a bigger device or a household's worth of chargers. Its shelves are designed to hold books and small display items.

The black finish blends into most rooms, and the lamp is easy to move since it has no table. Compared with the runjuly, it offers far fewer connections at a lower tier. We would choose it for a bedroom corner where light and one or two charging ports are enough.
products.bestFor: The lowest cost and a minimal charging setup
pros: Lowest cost tier of the five

buyingCriteria.explanation: Count the ports against the devices you own. The runjuly has two USB, one Type-C and two AC outlets, the SUNMORY has two USB and two outlets, and the Coucrek has only one USB and one Type-C. A phone and a tablet need two ports, but add a pair of earbuds, a reading light and a battery pack and you need more. Choose a lamp with at least one more port than you use today, and prefer one with Type-C if your newer devices use it.

The listings state 5V/2A on the ONEWISH and FOLKSMATE USB ports, which is a modest charging rate suited to phones and tablets rather than laptops. For a laptop, use the AC outlets on the runjuly, SUNMORY or ONEWISH instead of a USB port. Always check what your device needs before relying on a built-in port. Slow charging overnight is fine, but it will not top up a device quickly.

Guides suggest 400 to 800 lumens on a reading surface, and the SUNMORY's 800 lumen bulb sits at the top of that range. Adjustable color temperature lets you move from 3000K warm for relaxing to 4000K or higher for focused tasks. The ONEWISH covers 3000K to 6500K and the Coucrek uses an 11W bulb. Look for flicker-free light and a CRI of 80 or more if you read small print.

Every device charging from the lamp adds a cable, and loose cables are a trip hazard. Place the lamp so cables run toward the wall or furniture instead of across a walkway. Shelf lamps like the SUNMORY and FOLKSMATE can hang cables down the front, so use short charging cables. Also keep the main power cord out of walking paths.

A lamp with shelves and a tabletop is top-heavy, so tip-over risk matters. One guide suggests a base at least 8 inches across, and the load should be kept on lower shelves. The runjuly and ONEWISH use table bases that distribute weight, while the pole-and-shelf designs like the FOLKSMATE and Coucrek rely on a narrower footprint. Keep heavy books on the bottom tier and avoid placing the lamp where it can be bumped.

Touch dimming, like the FOLKSMATE's, is smooth but can fail with dry skin or poor circulation. Physical buttons on the pole are generally more dependable. Check where the switch sits, because a switch on the shade can be hard to reach beside a chair. A pull chain, rotary knob or a large button is easier on arthritic fingers than a touch pad.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging flexibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted the ports and outlets on each lamp, from the runjuly's five connections to the Coucrek's two. We also noted whether Type-C was included. The lamp with the most flexible mix of connections scored highest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Light output and adjustability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared bulb wattage and listed brightness, including the SUNMORY's 9W and 800 lumens and the Coucrek's 11W. We also checked for adjustable color temperature. Lamps that let you change warmth scored higher for reading.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability and layout
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at base design, shelf count and table size, comparing the runjuly's table base with the narrow pole of the Coucrek. Top-heavy lamps need a stable footprint, so buyer feedback about wobble informed this score.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of use
howWeEvaluated.description: We examined controls and assembly. The FOLKSMATE's touch dimming was weighed against physical switches on other lamps. Simple assembly and clear controls helped a lamp rank higher for our audience.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the tier
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared features to relative price tier, from the Coucrek at the lowest to the runjuly at the highest. The most capable lamp was weighed against the most basic, with port count and storage as the key difference.

howToChoose.subheading: For a Recliner or Sofa Side Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a surface at arm height, ports you can reach without bending and a stable base. A rounded edge helps if the lamp sits in a walkway. Make sure the switch is easy to reach from your seat.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The runjuly offers the most surface and ports, and the ONEWISH offers a round table. Both suit a recliner.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You charge many devices or want an end table replacement, as the runjuly offers. A higher tier buys ports and surface.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need only light and a couple of ports. The Coucrek at the lowest tier or the FOLKSMATE at a lower mid-range tier will do.

faq.q: Which lamp has the most charging ports?
faq.a: The runjuly has two USB ports, one Type-C port and two AC outlets, for five connections. The SUNMORY follows with two USB and two outlets. The Coucrek has the fewest with two.

faq.q: Are USB ports on a lamp fast enough to charge a tablet?
faq.a: Ports listed at 5V/2A are fine for phones and tablets overnight. They will be slow for larger devices. Use an AC outlet and your own charger for a laptop.
Yes, all five list an LED bulb included, with wattage from 9W to 11W. Check the color temperature options. You can swap in your own E26 bulb later if you prefer.

faq.q: Is a lamp with shelves safe if it is top-heavy?
faq.a: It is safe if you load it sensibly. Keep heavy items on the lower shelves and place the lamp where it will not be bumped. A wide base is better than a narrow one.

faq.q: How do I keep cables from becoming a trip hazard?
faq.a: Use short charging cables and run them toward the wall. Avoid stretching cables across walkways. A lamp tucked beside a chair is easier to manage than one in the middle of a room.

faq.q: Can I use a lamp with outlets for a heated item?
faq.a: Check the outlet rating before you plug in anything with a high wattage. Outlets on lamps are meant for small devices. Heating pads, space heaters and similar items should use a wall outlet.
